units.translation: A destructive vote will be cast against them
And he himself will prophesy this outrage against himself
Then I am devising a plot against myself
A mournful voice speaks of some dark mist throughout the house
For the people are fond of blaming their rulers
How utterly we are being destroyed here
Watching with keen eyes along my tracks
Hunters who have landed on the invisible track of the ship
Let it go with the wind
Row, my friends, with the wind of lamentation, beating the oar of your hands upon your heads
They raise a disorderly flight with the wind
Carried along by the ill-fated prayers of their father
According to the laws of suppliants
According to the laws of their homeland
That it is not by strength nor by force that one should prevail over the powerful, but by cunning
For self-will, when one thinks not rightly, is by itself no less strong than anything
What could I say or do to succeed, having directed my course to the one place where your bed holds you?
The sorrows at home by the hearth
The lots that fall to mortals
For they themselves have obtained by lot to manage all things among mortals
At the very tomb of Amphion, son of Diogenes
At the very tomb of wretched Lichas
Man against man was this one chosen
If, having come, he then speaks to my face (thus Bamberger for "will speak"), know well, and casts it before my eyes
Whom the lord himself chose according to their rank
When they came waging war because of envy of Theseus
Neither is it pleasant for me to speak, nor is it painless for you
To marry within one's own family
But his boast is beyond what a man should think
You speak kindly, as befits a prudent man
I say to honor me as a man, not as a god
He brings night and darkness before their eyes, and by day he is no more visible
Giving up their lives to pleasure day by day
with the wind, with a fair wind
in one point, in one respect
I throw down. I cover. I overpower. I destroy utterly
to throw down, to cast down
to throw down, to cast down
Having come, he will then speak to my face and cast it before my eyes

Καταβασμός [Katabasmós, "descent"], which is the Attic form, or Καταβαθμός [Katabathmós] in other writers, is the name of a sloping place that separates Egypt from Libya, about which see Strabo 17 p. 791 798 825 838 and others cited in the Thesaurus vol. 4 p. 1018: but Aeschylus speaks of the Καταδούποις [Katadoupois, "the Cataracts"] of the Nile, where that river rushes down from the mountains: which is clear from the passages of writers cited in the Thesaurus p. 1064.
For the Nile, beginning from the Cataracts
